subject: Efficient Data Augmentation for ZIP models

messages.author: 63cc02caac0434cf
messages.subject: Efficient Data Augmentation for ZIP models
parts:
Hello, 

I am trying to fit ZIP models in NIMBLE using data augmentation. For example, 

nimbleCode({
  beta0 ~ dflat()
  tau ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
  p ~dunif(0,1)
  psi[1:N] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:N], tau, zero_mean = 1)
  for(i in 1:N) {
    S[i] ~ dbern(p)
    mu[i] <- exp(log(E[i])+beta0 + psi[i])*(1-S[i]) +.001
    y[i] ~ dpois(mu[i])
  }
})

A disease mapping example. It works without issue but I plan to extend it to to a large data set and would like to make it more efficient. I know that S[i] can not be 1 when y[i]>0 so you only need to sample S[i] when y[i]=0. I am not sure the best way to implement this in Nimble. I know I can put S[i] to 0 in the model code but I would rather not do that since I think the model is written properly right now. I read about custom samplers but that seems like overkill. I just want S[i] to always to be 0 when y[i]>0. 

Also the full conditional probability S[i]=1 has a simple form p/(p+(1-p)exp(-mu[i])). I do not know if it is worth simplifying it or not using a custom sampler or if Nimble simplifies it like this. 

Thanks!

messages.author: f97d21be02e5ed9b
messages.subject: Re: Efficient Data Augmentation for ZIP models
parts:
A quick thought  - maybe the step function will come in handy here. step(x) = 0 if x < 0, 1 if x >= 0. 
so maybe instead of S[i]~dbern(p) you could do... 
S[i] ~ dbern(p*(1-step(y[i]-1))
If y = 0, step(-1) goes to 0, and p is multiplied by 1. If y = 1 or more, step(0, 1, etc) goes to 1 and p is multiplied by 0.

Something like that might do the trick.

-Heather

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Efficient Data Augmentation for ZIP models
parts:
Thanks for that suggestion, Heather.

Another way, which is used in other contexts, is to provide some S[i] values as data.  For i such that y[i] > 0, provide S[i] = 0 as data.  For other i, set S[i] to NA in the data vector you provide.  Those elements will be sampled by the MCMC.

This is also done in capture-recapture models in ecology.  When a capture history is 1 0 1 0 0 (1 = alive, 0 = dead, the sequence is over capture occasions through time), the latent state of whether the animal is alive or dead is known to be alive for the first three times but unknown for the last two times (after the last live capture).

-Perry
